explanation: Other sex chromosome disorders include Poly-X syndrome and Jacobs syndrome. Poly-X syndrome (or 'Super Female') is a female condition with three X chromosomes. They generally have no distinct features other than tending to be tall and thin, though some have learning difficulties. Their offspring usually have normal karyotypes. Having more than three X chromosomes is extremely rare and causes severe mental retardation. Jacobs syndrome occurs in males with an XYY karyotype, resulting from nondisjunction during spermatogenesis. It has a frequency of 1 in 1,000 males. Features include tall stature, persistent acne, and potential speech and reading difficulties, though affected individuals are fertile.

questions.q: What is the karyotype and typical appearance of a female with Poly-X (Super Female) syndrome?
opts: XO; broad chest and neck webbing.
XXX (3 copies of X); tall and thin with no other distinct physical features.
XXY; male appearance with underdeveloped testes.
questions.exp: Option B is correct because the slide describes Poly-X as: 'Super Female – 3 copies of X' with 'No distinct features, except tend to be tall and thin.'

questions.q: What is Jacobs syndrome, and what are its main features?
opts: An XO female condition; features underdeveloped ovaries.
An XYY male condition resulting from nondisjunction in spermatogenesis; features tall stature, persistent acne, and fertility.
An XXY male condition resulting from oogenesis errors; features breast development.
An XXXX female condition; features severe mental retardation.
questions.exp: Option B is correct because the slide defines Jacobs Syndrome as: 'XYY Males' that 'Results from nondisjunction in spermatogenesis' with features including 'Very tall; persistent acne' and 'are fertile.'
